A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniDomain with matching research identity, core framework, training corpus, and benchmark. All 16 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v2, including appendices and embedded figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 and Figures 3–5 report original results on 100 planning tasks and ablations of domain learning, fusion, and online planning.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original keyframe-validation examples, task-class results, and quantitative failure analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: New Section 5.1 adds automatic atomic-domain retrieval using LLM-inferred actions and top-K embedding matches, extending v1's manual retrieval. Section 4.2 also changes stated failure handling from restart to discard with possible restart. The central domain-learning, fusion, and planning pipeline remains intact.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds Agibot World demonstrations with human-annotated keyframes for validation. DROID pretraining and the 100-task planning benchmark covering BlockWorld, Desktop, Kitchen, and Combination remain.

E2.justification: The six planning baselines and the OP-S similarity-based keyframe comparator are retained. Figure 21 disaggregates the same planning comparisons. Newly specified SigLIP-2 implementation and baseline adaptations document existing comparisons without establishing comparator replacements.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces comparison of automatically selected keyframes against human annotations. The retained planning benchmark keeps its task count, metrics, GPT-4.1, and temperature 0.0. Teleoperation, judging procedures, and baseline budgets are newly disclosed settings, without evidence that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, Appendices C–F add verb-distribution analyses, keyframe-alignment checks, worked success/failure comparisons across all four task classes, and categorized domain-learning and online-planning failures. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages with standard errors in the benchmark and ablation figures. New Figure 21 follows the same practice. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation plots retain identical values, including 85% success and 83% optimality at K=0. V2 adds substantial task-class comparisons, keyframe-alignment findings, verb distributions, and failure breakdowns, including attribution of 53.4% of online failures to visual grounding in Appendix F.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the solvability definition from passing predicate set P_r to the solver in v1 to passing full domain D_r in v2, consistent with the surrounding procedure. Other core mathematics is retained. Appendix D's Parseval-based explanation supplies intuition rather than a formal semantic-boundary guarantee.

C1.justification: The three central contributions, zero-shot compositional-planning claim, and headline improvements of up to 58% in success and 160% in optimality remain. The introduction's high-level task-planning qualification clarifies the existing scope.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 explicitly delimits evaluation to high-level plans with teleoperated low-level control. Appendix D adds semantic and primitive-skill explanations, while Appendix F details failure mechanisms. The conclusion replaces manual retrieval as a limitation with redundancy and fusion costs arising from automatic retrieval.

D1.justification: V2 adds UniDomain and baseline prompt templates, ReAct controls, BoN-iVML adaptations, adaptive keyframe-window settings, hardware details, evaluation-judging procedures, and worked PDDL examples. These substantially expand reproducibility information. The project access address also changes; external resource availability was not verified.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds comparisons with Diehl et al. and Huang et al. concerning domain learning from limited demonstrations. Additional citations support evaluation practices, keyframe validation, and primitive-skill discussion. The principal positioning against handcrafted or narrowly learned domains remains.

P1.justification: Main section order and most existing prose are preserved. Changes include localized corrections and explanations, updated author/conference and acknowledgment text, a retrieval subsection, and reorganization of former Appendices A.1/A.2 into A/B alongside newly added appendix sections.

P2.justification: Figures 16–21 add distributions, a meta-domain graph, keyframe examples, energy curves, and task-class comparisons. Boxed PDDL and prompt displays substantially expand presentation. Original images are retained, but layouts change, including Figure 5 becoming full-width; Figure 15's instruction changes the destination drawer from yellow to orange.

improvement.justification: V1 leaves important execution, judging, and baseline-implementation details unspecified. V2 substantially addresses these transparency and reproducibility gaps through explicit teleoperation and human-verification disclosures, prompt templates, settings, and worked examples. Task-class results and failure analyses also make the retained performance claims more assessable. These gains are substantial despite unchanged headline scores; automatic retrieval remains separately unbenchmarked, and keyframe validation remains qualitative.
